answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any delivery disruption is costly, so switching primary vendor outright carries elevated risk despite the low-cost quote meeting the mandate on paper (memory_c2 only attests to cost and onboarding speed, not sustained delivery performance under tight capacity). Memory_c1 and memory_c4 indicate the incumbent relationship is stable and has previously yielded real margin recovery through renegotiation using market benchmarks, without introducing integration or delivery risk. Given the 14-day window and single decision slot, negotiating terms with the incumbent—using the low-cost vendor's quote as leverage—offers a path to narrow or close the cost gap while preserving delivery continuity. This defers the higher-risk switch decision rather than committing to it under time pressure. I verified memory_c2 and memory_c4 to confirm the original records support cost outcomes for switching versus negotiating before committing, since these two memories most directly bear on the cost-versus-risk tradeoff at stake.
